court.case: Truchon and Gladu v Canada (AG) and Quebec (AG)
court.what: Struck federal RFND and Quebec end-of-life criteria as unjustifiable Charter limits (ss. 7 and 15); suspended invalidity 6 months

non_appeal.actor: Government of Canada / Minister of Justice David Lametti

primary.quote: The Government of Canada did not appeal the Québec Superior Court decision in Truchon and Gladu [Truchon], which declared the “reasonable foreseeability of natural death” eligibility requirement to be an unjustifiable limit on section 7 and 15 Charter rights.

non_appeal.thesis: Canadian cabinet chose legislation over SCC appeal — the hinge that unlocked Track 2 drafting

effects: Two safeguard tracks (death foreseeable vs not)
Sole mental illness excluded at assent; sunset / later schedule via Senate path
Waiver of final consent for some foreseeable-death cases
senate_notes: Wallin advance-request amendment adopted in Senate then largely refused by Commons
Gold: rushing advance requests into C-7 without study would be irresponsible
Kutcher: mental-illness exclusion sunset amendment path

honest_non_edge.PASS: Non-appeal + C-7 = Canadian political sequence after Truchon
honest_non_edge.FAIL: Foreign court or CCP ordered Track 2
